title: Making a file on a disk
question: The same create, on ext4: what does a disk file system keep track of?
text: The same create as in memory, but on ext4. A disk file system has to keep track of what it used.
1. [ext4_create](1:ext4_create) makes the file, all inside one journal transaction, so that a crash leaves all of it or none of it.
2. [__ext4_new_inode](1:__ext4_new_inode) finds a free inode in a block group's inode bitmap and marks it used.
3. [add_dirent_to_buf](1:add_dirent_to_buf) writes the name "new.txt" into free space in a block of the directory, next to the other names.

Try: [a file in a directory that does not exist](try:1): the lookup fails before ext4_create ever runs. Then look at the in-memory create example next to [this one's calls](1:ext4_create:calls): how much more a disk file system does.
